tone_statements.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2019. Proper names and case markers in Sinyar (Chad/Sudan). STUF - Language Typology and Universals 72(4): 467-504. (HAL author manuscript halshs-03096955, 29 pp.)
tone_statements.quote: iv.) Sinyar has a system of two contrastive level tones (Low/High, more briefly L/H). Moreover, frequent downsteps (marked by ꜝ ) are attached to a lexical unit and may appear, especially between two successive L tones, at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end of the word. … As for final downsteps (e.g. ùmmàꜝ ‘woman’, ɓìsìꜝ ‘dog’), they do not have a systematic impact on the following unit but their influence is limited to the initial L of the different clitics that may be suffixed to them.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.2 'Typological features', item iv, ms p. 3 (examples 1-4 continue to ms p. 5), (HAL author version)

tone_statements.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2019. Le système tonal du sinyar (langue du Darfour occidental). Paper presented at the Séminaire du LLACAN, Villejuif (CNRS-LLACAN), 5 June 2019. Abstract published in: Meddour, Tahar, 'Séminaire du LLACAN : Le système tonal du sinyar (Pascal Boyeldieu)', Blog du LLACAN, 28 May 2019. No handout or slides deposited (HAL, LLACAN author page checked 2026-09-22).
tone_statements.quote: Langue présumée SBB (Soudanique central), le sinyar se caractérise par un système tonal atypique, opposant deux tons (H/B) et marqué par de nombreuses failles tonales, précédant ton bas à l’initiale du mot ou suivant ton bas à la finale du mot. Il détaillera ces contextes ainsi que les effets de la faille dans chacun des cas.
tone_statements.translation: A presumed SBB (Central Sudanic) language, Sinyar is characterised by an atypical tonal system, opposing two tones (H/L) and marked by numerous tonal downsteps ('failles tonales'), preceding a low tone at the beginning of the word or following a low tone at the end of the word. He will detail these contexts as well as the effects of the downstep in each case.
tone_statements.locator: seminar abstract (blog post body, paragraph after the title line)
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones (H, L) with frequent lexical downsteps attached to words (word-initial before L, word-final after L, rarely internal); downsteps lower following L-toned clitics; no stress or accent mentioned.

sources.note: Sinyar has two contrastive tones H vs L (B) and numerous lexical downsteps ('failles tonales') located word-initially before an L or word-finally after an L; the talk was devoted entirely to these downstep contexts and their effects. Consistent with the fuller passages in our read rows (Boyeldieu 2015 sec. 2; 2019 STUF sec. 2.2 iv: two level tones L/H, downsteps initial/internal/final, effect on L-toned clitics). Only the abstract is available; it says nothing about stress.
